target: scripts/check_pr_gates.py — pre-merge guard: refuse to merge a PR whose gates run never ran or did not pass
findings_summary: NO DATABASE ACCESS — this script queries the GitHub REST API only, so the schema/join/timeout sections of the protocol do not apply. Root cause established by measurement, not inference: a PR whose mergeable state is CONFLICTING gets NO GitHub Actions run at all, because pull_request workflows execute against the merge commit and that commit cannot be built. Proven on PR #907 — 40+ minutes with zero runs while CONFLICTING; rebased to clear the conflict; run appeared 20 seconds later and all five jobs passed. Same explanation retro-fits PR #902, whose run appeared minutes after its rebase, not after the close/reopen I had credited. Real fix is branch protection requiring the gates checks, but repos/lmcdo/nswcompliance/branches/main/protection returns HTTP 403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro — unavailable on a private repo on the free plan. Existing mitigation confirmed live: gates also runs on push to main (04:30:03Z after the 04:30:00Z merge, success) and main-red-alarm sweeps for a HEAD with no successful run, so an unchecked merge is caught AFTER landing. The remaining gap is purely pre-merge, which is what this script covers.
